key_insight: An independent compliance-damage field lets sharp cohesive cracks emerge at finite phase-field length while keeping the phase-field continuous.
engineering_relevance: The formulation supports large-deformation fracture modeling with independently prescribed bulk material behavior and mixed-mode traction–separation laws.
method: Separate crack geometry from material degradation using an independent compliance-damage field.
Use a rank-one additive deformation-gradient split to represent crack separation and orientation.
Couple bulk deformation, crack opening, and crack-plane rotation through minimum potential energy.
evidence_signal: One-dimensional energy comparisons favor concentrated cracks, while 2D and 3D examples demonstrate finite-deformation behavior and near-tip stresses closely matching the analytical 1/r asymptote outside the cohesive zone.
watch_item: Numerical implementation must resolve concentrated compliance damage and crack strain; the abstract does not establish mesh sensitivity or computational cost.
paper_title: A variational phase-field theory of cohesive fracture at finite deformation
